documents.citation: Upton Sinclair, The Jungle, Chapter XIV, 1906. Project Gutenberg / Library of Congress.
documents.excerpt: There were the men in the pickle rooms, for instance, where old Antanas had gotten his death; scarce a one of these that had not some spot of horror on his person. Let a man so much as scrape his finger pushing a truck in the pickle rooms, and he might have a sore that would put him out of the world; all the joints in his fingers might be eaten by the acid, one by one. Of the butchers and floorsmen, the beef-boners and trimmers, and all those who used knives, you could scarcely find a person who had the use of his thumb; time and again the base of it had been slashed, till it was a mere lump of flesh against which the man pressed the knife to hold it.

documents.citation: Ida M. Tarbell, The History of the Standard Oil Company, Volume II, Chapter XXVI, 1904. Originally published by McClure's Magazine; available through the Library of Congress.
documents.excerpt: If the Standard Oil Company or its officers had been brought to trial on charges of violating the Interstate Commerce Act... it is probable that they would have been punished for some of these practices. But such a trial was never had. The reason generally given for the failure of the government to act was that Congress had not yet passed the legislation which would make such prosecution possible — but that the legislation had not been passed was due in large measure to the influence of the Standard itself upon Congress.

documents.citation: Theodore Roosevelt, Message to Congress on the Pure Food and Drug Legislation, June 1906. National Archives, Presidential Messages to Congress.
documents.excerpt: I recommend that a law be enacted to regulate interstate commerce in misbranded and adulterated foods, drinks, and drugs. Such a law would protect legitimate manufacture and commerce, and would tend to secure the health and welfare of the consuming public. The Federal inspection of meats should be thorough enough to guarantee that no diseased, filthy, or unwholesome product reaches the consumer... The revelations made by recent investigations make it evident that we cannot rely upon State laws or State officials alone.
